24. ... P × P
25. Q × P ch K — K 3
26. Q — Kt 4 ch K — B 3
27. Q — Kt 5 ch K — K 3
28. Q × P Q — Q 3
29. P — B 5 Q — Q 4
30. P — K 4! Q — Q 8 ch
31. K — R 2 P — B 3
32. Q — Kt 4 ch! K — K 2
33. Kt × P Q × Q
34. Kt × Q Kt — K 3
35. P — K 5 P × P
36. Kt × P Kt — Q 5

The game went on for a few more moves, and, there being no way to counteract the advance of White's two passed Pawns, Black resigned.

GAME 4. FRENCH DEFENCE
(St. Petersburg, 1913)

White: J. R. Capablanca. Black: E. A. Snosko-Borovski.

1. P — Q 4 P — K 3
2. P — K 4 P — Q 4
3. Kt — Q B 3 Kt — K B 3
4. B — Kt 5 B — Kt 5

This constitutes the McCutcheon Variation. It aims at taking the initiative away from White. Instead
